codec: the BSON codec the server is built with (the encoder and decoder every wire frame passes through)

limits.depth_rule: the root document has depth 1; each embedded document or array adds 1; a decoder refuses depth 101 (driver-python-spec section 7.2)

value_forms.$binary: {"$binary": {"hex": "00ff", "subType": "04"}}: BSON binary; subType is two hex digits; hex is the payload ("" for empty).
value_forms.$doc: a document: {"$doc": [[key, value], ...]}, an ordered list of [key, value] pairs. Order is the wire order and a key may repeat (decode/duplicate-keys); a plain JSON object is never a document in this file.
value_forms.$numberDecimal: {"$numberDecimal": "1.50"}: BSON decimal128 (BID), as the canonical decimal string; the exponent and trailing zeros are part of the value ("1.50" and "1.5" are different bytes). "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity" and "-0" are legal.
value_forms.$numberDouble: {"$numberDouble": "1.5"}: BSON double, the shortest decimal that round-trips, or "NaN" (the quiet NaN 0x7ff8000000000000), "Infinity", "-Infinity", "-0" (negative zero). Parse with a correctly rounded parser.
value_forms.$numberLong: {"$numberLong": "-5"}: BSON int64, a decimal string. An int64 stays int64 even when the number fits int32.
value_forms.array: an array is a JSON array of typed values.
value_forms.string: a string is a JSON string (\u0000 is a NUL character). Encode vectors hold valid Unicode only.

kinds.datetime_floor: instant -> expected_millis. A time with sub-millisecond digits becomes milliseconds by flooring toward negative infinity (never truncating toward zero); hex is the document {"t": <that datetime>} the server's time encoder wrote.
kinds.decode: hex -> document. Bytes the server's decoder accepts, read to the typed document; reencodes_identically says whether writing that document gives the same bytes (false for a non-canonical input). last_wins_document, when present, is the document as a mapping that keeps the last of a repeated key (position of the first).
kinds.encode: document -> hex. The codec must write exactly these bytes for the typed document, and read them back to the same typed document.
kinds.encode_refuse: document -> refusal. An encoder must refuse to write the typed document (InvalidArgumentError, before any byte is written). server_encoder records what the server's encoder does.
kinds.reject: hex -> refusal. A decoder must refuse the bytes with the refusal class named (ProtocolError, driver-python-spec section 7.2), never crash, hang or raise a language-level exception. server_decoder records what the server's own decoder does with the same bytes: "accepted" marks an input the spec is stricter about than the server.
kinds.size: recipe -> document_bytes, sha256. A document too large to list as hex: build {key: fill repeated fill_bytes times}, encode it, and the bytes must have this length and SHA-256. fits_one_frame and within_default_document_limit say where it sits against the limits.

vectors.name: int64/zero
vectors.notes: an int64 stays int64 even when it fits int32; a Python int in the int32 range is written int32 (a $numberInt), not this.

vectors.name: int64/small
vectors.notes: an int64 that fits int32, kept int64.

vectors.name: int64/just-over-int32
vectors.notes: 2^31: the first value that needs int64.

vectors.name: int64/just-under-int32
vectors.notes: -2^31-1: the first negative value that needs int64.

vectors.name: double/negative-zero
vectors.notes: bytes 8000000000000000: -0.0 and 0.0 are different bytes.

vectors.name: double/point-one
vectors.notes: not exactly representable: the bytes are the nearest double.

vectors.name: double/nan
vectors.notes: the quiet NaN 0x7ff8000000000000, which is what Python's float('nan') writes; Go's math.NaN() is 0x7ff8000000000001, so this vector builds the bits explicitly.

vectors.name: double/subnormal-smallest
vectors.notes: 5e-324, the smallest positive subnormal (bits 0000000000000001).

vectors.name: double/subnormal-largest
vectors.notes: the largest subnormal.

vectors.name: double/min-normal
vectors.notes: the smallest positive normal double.

vectors.name: double/max
vectors.notes: the largest finite double.

vectors.name: double/2^53-1
vectors.notes: 9007199254740991, the largest integer every double below it also represents.

vectors.name: double/2^53+2
vectors.notes: 9007199254740994: 2^53+1 has no double, the next one is +2 (float(2**53+1) is 2^53).

vectors.name: string/multibyte-3-byte
vectors.notes: three CJK characters, 3 bytes each.

vectors.name: string/multibyte-4-byte
vectors.notes: U+1F600, outside the basic plane (a surrogate pair in UTF-16).

vectors.name: string/max-codepoint
vectors.notes: U+10FFFF.

vectors.name: string/noncharacter
vectors.notes: U+FFFE is a valid scalar value.

vectors.name: string/embedded-nul
vectors.notes: a string may hold NUL: the length prefix, not a terminator, delimits it (the server's encoder allows it).

vectors.name: string/long-300
vectors.notes: longer than 255 bytes.

vectors.name: datetime/minus-one-ms
vectors.notes: 1969-12-31T23:59:59.999Z: a value below zero is -1, not 0 (see the datetime_floor vectors for how a driver gets it from an instant).

vectors.name: datetime/python-max
vectors.notes: 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z, datetime.max at millisecond precision (253402300799999).

vectors.name: datetime/over-python-max
vectors.notes: one millisecond past Python's datetime.max: a Python decoder returns Opaque (driver-python-spec section 7.2), never OverflowError.

vectors.name: datetime/under-python-min
vectors.notes: one millisecond before datetime.min: Opaque in Python.

vectors.name: datetime/int64-max
vectors.notes: the largest datetime BSON holds.

vectors.name: datetime/int64-min
vectors.notes: the smallest datetime BSON holds.

vectors.name: binary/generic-empty
vectors.notes: subtype 00, no bytes.

vectors.name: binary/generic
vectors.notes: subtype 00.

vectors.name: binary/uuid-subtype-4
vectors.notes: a UUID: subtype 04, 16 bytes in RFC 4122 order.

vectors.name: binary/subtype-01-function

vectors.name: binary/subtype-03-uuid-legacy
vectors.notes: the legacy UUID subtype; not a Python UUID.

vectors.name: binary/generic-4096
vectors.notes: a payload past one byte of length.

vectors.name: decimal128/zero-with-exponent
vectors.notes: zero with a positive exponent keeps the exponent.

vectors.name: decimal128/one-point-five-zero
vectors.notes: trailing zeros are part of the value: 1.50 and 1.5 are different bytes.

vectors.name: decimal128/max-digits

vectors.name: decimal128/max-digits-fraction

vectors.name: decimal128/exponent-max

vectors.name: decimal128/exponent-min
vectors.notes: the smallest exponent (a subnormal-style value).

vectors.name: decimal128/largest-finite
vectors.notes: 34 nines at the largest exponent.

vectors.name: timestamp/typical

vectors.name: timestamp/max

vectors.notes: Opaque in Python.

vectors.name: document/key-order
vectors.notes: keys are written in the order given, never sorted.

vectors.name: document/empty-key
vectors.notes: the empty string is a legal key.

vectors.name: document/key-multibyte
vectors.notes: keys are UTF-8.

vectors.name: document/key-dollar-dot
vectors.notes: the codec gives $ and . no meaning.

vectors.name: document/key-long
vectors.notes: a 300-byte key.

vectors.name: document/nested-depth-100
vectors.notes: the deepest document a decoder must accept (the root counts 1).

vectors.name: array/ints
vectors.notes: array keys are the decimal indexes 0, 1, 2.

vectors.name: array/mixed
vectors.notes: an array holds any types, in order.

vectors.name: array/eleven-elements
vectors.notes: keys 0 to 10: the index key grows to two digits.

vectors.name: array/nested-depth-100
vectors.notes: arrays nested to the deepest depth a decoder must accept (the root document counts 1).

vectors.name: document/realistic-row
vectors.notes: a stored document as a find returns it: _id_ first (wire.md).

vectors.name: document/every-type
vectors.notes: one document with every type, in this order.

vectors.name: decode/duplicate-keys
vectors.notes: a repeated key: the server's ordered decoder keeps both; into a map the last wins (last_wins_document). A decoder returning a mapping must take the last value.

vectors.name: decode/array-keys-out-of-order
vectors.notes: array element keys are ignored on read: the elements come back in wire order whatever their keys say.

vectors.name: decode/array-keys-non-numeric
vectors.notes: keys that are not indexes are ignored too.

vectors.name: decode/array-keys-gap
vectors.notes: keys 0 and 2: positions are wire order, not the keys.

vectors.name: decode/double-nan-payload
vectors.notes: a NaN with a payload (0x7ff8000000000001, what Go's math.NaN writes) reads as NaN.

vectors.name: decode/double-negative-nan
vectors.notes: the sign bit set (0xfff8000000000000) is still NaN.

vectors.name: decode/double-signaling-nan
vectors.notes: a signaling NaN (0x7ff0000000000001) is NaN.

vectors.name: decode/boolean-0-and-1
vectors.notes: the only two legal boolean bytes.

vectors.name: decode/binary-subtype-2-old
vectors.notes: the deprecated old binary subtype carries an inner length; the decoder returns the payload without it.

vectors.name: decode/binary-subtype-4-wrong-length
vectors.notes: a UUID subtype with 15 bytes: the server's decoder takes any length. driver-python-spec section 7.2 is silent; a Python decoder must not raise a language-level exception (return Opaque).

vectors.name: decode/regex-options-unsorted
vectors.notes: options are kept as written.

vectors.name: decode/int32-negative
vectors.notes: two's complement.

vectors.name: decode/string-nul-in-value
vectors.notes: a NUL inside a string value is data.

vectors.name: reject/empty-input
vectors.notes: no bytes at all.

vectors.name: reject/truncated-header
vectors.notes: three bytes: the length prefix itself is cut.

vectors.name: reject/length-zero
vectors.notes: declared length 0.

vectors.name: reject/length-4
vectors.notes: declared length 4 (the smallest document is 5).

vectors.name: reject/length-negative
vectors.notes: declared length -1 (0xffffffff).

vectors.name: reject/length-int32-min
vectors.notes: declared length -2^31.

vectors.name: reject/length-too-long
vectors.notes: the declared length is one more than the bytes given.

vectors.name: reject/length-huge
vectors.notes: declared length 2^31-1 over a 12-byte buffer: a decoder must not allocate or read that much.

vectors.name: reject/length-too-short

vectors.name: reject/trailing-garbage
vectors.notes: a complete document followed by one byte: the declared length must equal the bytes consumed.

vectors.name: reject/trailing-zero
vectors.notes: a complete document followed by a second terminator.

vectors.name: reject/two-documents
vectors.notes: two complete documents back to back.

vectors.name: reject/missing-terminator

vectors.name: reject/missing-terminator-header-only
vectors.notes: length 5 and a non-zero last byte.

vectors.name: reject/int32-truncated
vectors.notes: an int32 element with a 3-byte body, length consistent.

vectors.name: reject/int64-truncated
vectors.notes: an int64 element with a 7-byte body.

vectors.name: reject/double-truncated
vectors.notes: a double element with a 7-byte body.

vectors.name: reject/datetime-truncated
vectors.notes: a datetime element with a 7-byte body.

vectors.name: reject/timestamp-truncated
vectors.notes: a timestamp element with a 7-byte body.

vectors.name: reject/objectid-truncated
vectors.notes: an object id with an 11-byte body.

vectors.name: reject/decimal128-truncated

vectors.name: reject/boolean-byte-2
vectors.notes: a boolean whose byte is 2: only 0 and 1 are legal.

vectors.name: reject/unknown-type-0x20
vectors.notes: type byte 0x20 is not a BSON type, so the element has no length. driver-python-spec section 7.2 does not list it; refuse it.

vectors.name: reject/unknown-type-0x14
vectors.notes: type byte 0x14 is not a BSON type.

vectors.name: reject/key-unterminated
vectors.notes: an element key with no NUL before the end of the document.

vectors.name: reject/string-length-zero
vectors.notes: a string declared with length 0 (the minimum is 1, the NUL).

vectors.name: reject/string-length-negative
vectors.notes: a string declared with length -1.

vectors.name: reject/string-length-beyond-document
vectors.notes: a string declared far longer than the document.

vectors.name: reject/string-missing-nul
vectors.notes: a string whose last counted byte is not NUL.

vectors.name: reject/string-invalid-utf8
vectors.notes: a string value holding the byte 0xff. The server accepts this input; the spec is stricter than the server here, and the in-tree codecs follow the spec.

vectors.name: reject/string-overlong-utf8
vectors.notes: an overlong encoding of NUL (0xc0 0x80). The server accepts this input; the spec is stricter than the server here, and the in-tree codecs follow the spec.

vectors.name: reject/string-truncated-utf8
vectors.notes: a three-byte sequence cut after two bytes. The server accepts this input; the spec is stricter than the server here, and the in-tree codecs follow the spec.

vectors.name: reject/string-lone-surrogate
vectors.notes: a UTF-16 surrogate encoded in three bytes (0xed 0xa0 0x80): not valid UTF-8. The server accepts this input; the spec is stricter than the server here, and the in-tree codecs follow the spec.

vectors.name: reject/string-above-max-codepoint
vectors.notes: 0xf4 0x90 0x80 0x80 is a code point above U+10FFFF. The server accepts this input; the spec is stricter than the server here, and the in-tree codecs follow the spec.

vectors.name: reject/key-invalid-utf8
vectors.notes: an element key holding the byte 0xff. The server accepts this input; the spec is stricter than the server here, and the in-tree codecs follow the spec.

vectors.name: reject/javascript-invalid-utf8
vectors.notes: a JavaScript element whose code is not UTF-8. The server accepts this input; the spec is stricter than the server here, and the in-tree codecs follow the spec.

vectors.notes: an embedded document whose declared length is 6 over a 12-byte body.

vectors.notes: an embedded document whose last byte is not the terminator.

vectors.name: reject/nested-trailing-garbage

vectors.name: reject/depth-101-documents
vectors.notes: documents nested to depth 101 (the root counts 1): over the limit of 100.

vectors.name: reject/depth-101-arrays
vectors.notes: arrays nested to depth 101.

vectors.notes: documents nested to depth 1000: a recursive decoder must stop long before the language's own recursion limit.

vectors.notes: a key may not hold NUL: a key is a BSON cstring, and a NUL would end it early and shift every later byte (driver-python-spec section 7.2).

vectors.notes: the epoch.

vectors.name: datetime_floor/1969-12-31T23:59:59.9995Z

vectors.notes: floors down, not toward the epoch.

vectors.name: datetime_floor/1969-12-31T23:59:59.0005Z
vectors.notes: -999.5 ms floors to -1000.

vectors.name: datetime_floor/2026-10-13T12:34:56.7895Z
vectors.notes: after the epoch the floor is the truncation.
